subject: general
question: Find the area of a rhombus of side 17 cm with one of its diagonal 16 cm long.
solution:
Given:

Length of side = 17 cm

Length of a diagonal = 16 cm

Concept used:

The two diagonals bisect each other at 90° in a rhombus.

Formula used:

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × Product of the two diagonals

Calculations:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d96e07cc667184b8460c766ec9afc7d09c782340bb654476197c0b883a5f4001.png] 

Let AC = 16 cm and BD = x cm

If the two diagonals of rhombus ABCD intersect at O then,

⇒ AO2 + BO2 = AB2

⇒ (16/2)2 + (x/2)2 = 172

⇒ 64 + (x2/4) = 289

⇒ (x2/4) = 225

⇒ x2 = 900

⇒ x = 30 cm

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × 16 × 30

⇒ 8 × 30

⇒ 240 cm2

∴ The area of the rhombus is 240 cm2
